In detail

Södermalm is one of Stockholm's 11 official stadsdelsnamnder (city district committees). Bra (Brottsforebyggande radet), Sweden's national crime-prevention council, recorded 32,269 total reported offences here in 2025, across a population of 130,402 residents (Stockholms stad, 31 December 2024) — a rate of 24,746 offences per 100,000 residents, close to the citywide average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. Sodermalm is one of Stockholm's most visited nightlife and restaurant districts (SoFo, Hornstull, Slussen) — it draws far more people through it than its resident count alone would suggest, which pushes its per-resident rate up without that meaning elevated risk per visit. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Stockholm — real Bra / Stockholms stad figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Södermalm safe?

Wandroz currently rates Södermalm in Stockholm, Sweden as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Stockholm, Sweden, based on Brå (Brottsförebyggande rådet)'s 2025 reported-offence data. This source has no time-of-day breakdown, so this is one overall level rather than a separately measured day and night figure — see the note on this page before treating the day/night badges as independently measured.

Does Södermalm's rating cover night-time safety specifically?

Not separately. Brå (Brottsförebyggande rådet)'s 2025 reported-offence data publishes one figure per zone with no time-of-day split, so Södermalm's day and night badges show the same underlying level rather than an independently measured night figure. Treat it as a general indicator, not a night-specific measurement.

Is Södermalm a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Södermalm's rating is a useful general indicator, but this data is normalised against registered residents, not visitor footfall — busy tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher without that meaning elevated risk for a visitor passing through. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.

What official data is Södermalm's rating based on?

Brå (Brottsförebyggande rådet)'s 2025 reported-offence data, covering Södermalm's real administrative boundary. This is a genuine official dataset, not a qualitative judgment or press research — see the methodology page for the exact figures, the year they cover, and how the rate is calculated.
